# Multi Search Engine v2.0.1

Integration of 17 search engines for web crawling without API keys.

## Search Engines

### Domestic (8)
- **Baidu**: `https://www.baidu.com/s?wd={keyword}`
- **Bing CN**: `https://cn.bing.com/search?q={keyword}&ensearch=0`
- **Bing INT**: `https://cn.bing.com/search?q={keyword}&ensearch=1`
- **360**: `https://www.so.com/s?q={keyword}`
- **Sogou**: `https://sogou.com/web?query={keyword}`
- **WeChat**: `https://wx.sogou.com/weixin?type=2&query={keyword}`
- **Toutiao**: `https://so.toutiao.com/search?keyword={keyword}`
- **Jisilu**: `https://www.jisilu.cn/explore/?keyword={keyword}`

### International (9)
- **Google**: `https://www.google.com/search?q={keyword}`
- **Google HK**: `https://www.google.com.hk/search?q={keyword}`
- **DuckDuckGo**: `https://duckduckgo.com/html/?q={keyword}`
- **Yahoo**: `https://search.yahoo.com/search?p={keyword}`
- **Startpage**: `https://www.startpage.com/sp/search?query={keyword}`
- **Brave**: `https://search.brave.com/search?q={keyword}`
- **Ecosia**: `https://www.ecosia.org/search?q={keyword}`
- **Qwant**: `https://www.qwant.com/?q={keyword}`
- **WolframAlpha**: `https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i={keyword}`

## Quick Examples

```javascript
// Basic search
web_fetch({"url": "https://www.google.com/search?q=python+tutorial"})

// Site-specific
web_fetch({"url": "https://www.google.com/search?q=site:github.com+react"})

// File type
web_fetch({"url": "https://www.google.com/search?q=machine+learning+filetype:pdf"})

// Time filter (past week)
web_fetch({"url": "https://www.google.com/search?q=ai+news&tbs=qdr:w"})

// Privacy search
web_fetch({"url": "https://duckduckgo.com/html/?q=privacy+tools"})

// DuckDuckGo Bangs
web_fetch({"url": "https://duckduckgo.com/html/?q=!gh+tensorflow"})

// Knowledge calculation
web_fetch({"url": "https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=100+USD+to+CNY"})
```

## Advanced Operators

| Operator | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `site:` | `site:github.com python` | Search within site |
| `filetype:` | `filetype:pdf report` | Specific file type |
| `""` | `"machine learning"` | Exact match |
| `-` | `python -snake` | Exclude term |
| `OR` | `cat OR dog` | Either term |

## Time Filters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `tbs=qdr:h` | Past hour |
| `tbs=qdr:d` | Past day |
| `tbs=qdr:w` | Past week |
| `tbs=qdr:m` | Past month |
| `tbs=qdr:y` | Past year |

## Privacy Engines

- **DuckDuckGo**: No tracking
- **Startpage**: Google results + privacy
- **Brave**: Independent index
- **Qwant**: EU GDPR compliant

## Bangs Shortcuts (DuckDuckGo)

| Bang | Destination |
|------|-------------|
| `!g` | Google |
| `!gh` | GitHub |
| `!so` | Stack Overflow |
| `!w` | Wikipedia |
| `!yt` | YouTube |

## WolframAlpha Queries

- Math: `integrate x^2 dx`
- Conversion: `100 USD to CNY`
- Stocks: `AAPL stock`
- Weather: `weather in Beijing`

Grey Goose (French pronunciation: [[ɡʁe ɡus]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French))[[1]](#cite_note-1) is a brand of [vodka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodka) produced in France. It was created in the 1990s by American businessman and philanthropist [Sidney Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Frank), who sold it to the multinational company [Bacardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacardi)[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) in 2004. The Maître de Chai for Grey Goose is [François Thibault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Thibault), who developed the original recipe for the vodka in [Cognac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognac,_France).

## Creation and company history
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Grey_Goose_(vodka)&action=edit&section=1)]

{{cite magazine\n | last = Stevenson\n | first = Seth\n | title = The Cocktail Creationist\n | url = https://nymag.com/nymetro/news/bizfinance/biz/features/10816/\n | magazine = [[New York (magazine)|New York]]\n | date = December 30, 2004\n | access-date = February 23, 2026\n}}"}},"i":0}}]}">

“I remember there was always something in the name that had magic with the consumer[...]"

"People are always looking for something new."

— Sidney Frank on his vodka[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)

Grey Goose was created by Sidney Frank Importing Co (SFIC). [Sidney Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Frank), founder/CEO of the company, developed the idea in the summer of 1997. SFIC partnered with cognac producer [François Thibault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Thibault) in France to transition his skills from [cognac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognac_(drink)) to vodka production, of which Frank directed his team to "come back with a vodka."[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)

The company selected France due to the country's [culinary history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_cuisine) and sophisticated prestige, as well as to differentiate itself from other vodkas produced in Eastern Europe. The company also developed its distinctive [smoked glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoked_glass) bottle, featuring French [geese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geese) in flight, and delivered its product in wooden [crates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crate) to evoke a presentation that was similar to wine. Likewise, the tall and crystal-clear bottles would be prominent and displayed as such at bars.[[4]](#cite_note-Rendon-4)[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)
In 1998, the [Beverage Testing Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverage_Tasting_Institute#Beverage_Testing_Institute) reviewed Grey Goose Vodka, and the brand received a score of 96 out of 100.[[5]](#cite_note-5) In 2001, Grey Goose released its first flavor, L'Orange, followed by Le Citron in 2002.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

The company was eventually sold by Sidney Frank to [Bacardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacardi) for a reported US$2.2 billion in 2004.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) Grey Goose was the best-selling [premium brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top-shelf_Liquor) vodka in the United States,[[4]](#cite_note-Rendon-4) selling more than 1.5 million cases that year.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Grey Goose partnered with entertainer [Jamie Foxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Foxx) for a nine-part online series called Off Script.[[8]](#cite_note-8) It is the official vodka of the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_(tennis)) tennis tournament, and is the key ingredient in the "[honey deuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_deuce)," the signature drink of the tournament.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

## Product description
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Grey_Goose_(vodka)&action=edit&section=2)]

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grey_Goose_Vodka_IMG_3297.JPGA bottle of Grey Goose vodka, from 2010
The wheat used in the creation of Grey Goose vodka is grown in the [Picardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picardy) region of France. It is distilled in the [Northeast of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris), then sent to Cognac, France. Once received, the [distillate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distillate) is blended with a mix of [spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_water) and [bottled water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottled_water). Grey Goose uses "soft [winter wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_wheat)",[[10]](#cite_note-10) sown in October and harvested in August, which provides it with four additional months of growth in comparison to [summer wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_wheat).

Although Grey Goose distills its vodka from wheat, the product is overall [gluten-free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluten-free).[[11]](#cite_note-11) The distillation process removes the gluten from the final product.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

During the distilling process, Grey Goose uses [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme)[[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid_weasel_words)] to break down [carbohydrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbohydrates) into fermentable sugars. The [fermentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermentation) takes place continuously over six [cascading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascading) tanks, producing a 20-[proof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_(alcohol)) beer. The "wash" is then distilled into [spirits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquor) using a five-step process. The water used in the vodka comes from a natural spring 150 meters (500 feet) below the blending facility in Cognac, which is lined with [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone), providing [calcium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium)-rich spring water; that water is then filtered to remove impurities. After the filtration, the vodka is bottled in-plant. Grey Goose vodka is bottled with a replaceable [cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_cork) rather than a [screw cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screw_cap).[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-men-14)

“I remember there was always something in the name that had magic with the consumer[...]"

"People are always looking for something new."

— Sidney Frank on his vodka[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)

Grey Goose was created by Sidney Frank Importing Co (SFIC). [Sidney Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Frank), founder/CEO of the company, developed the idea in the summer of 1997. SFIC partnered with cognac producer [François Thibault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Thibault) in France to transition his skills from [cognac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognac_(drink)) to vodka production, of which Frank directed his team to "come back with a vodka."[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)

The company selected France due to the country's [culinary history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_cuisine) and sophisticated prestige, as well as to differentiate itself from other vodkas produced in Eastern Europe. The company also developed its distinctive [smoked glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoked_glass) bottle, featuring French [geese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geese) in flight, and delivered its product in wooden [crates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crate) to evoke a presentation that was similar to wine. Likewise, the tall and crystal-clear bottles would be prominent and displayed as such at bars.[[4]](#cite_note-Rendon-4)[[3]](#cite_note-NYMag-3)
In 1998, the [Beverage Testing Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverage_Tasting_Institute#Beverage_Testing_Institute) reviewed Grey Goose Vodka, and the brand received a score of 96 out of 100.[[5]](#cite_note-5) In 2001, Grey Goose released its first flavor, L'Orange, followed by Le Citron in 2002.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

The company was eventually sold by Sidney Frank to [Bacardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacardi) for a reported US$2.2 billion in 2004.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) Grey Goose was the best-selling [premium brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top-shelf_Liquor) vodka in the United States,[[4]](#cite_note-Rendon-4) selling more than 1.5 million cases that year.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Grey Goose partnered with entertainer [Jamie Foxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Foxx) for a nine-part online series called Off Script.[[8]](#cite_note-8) It is the official vodka of the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_(tennis)) tennis tournament, and is the key ingredient in the "[honey deuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_deuce)," the signature drink of the tournament.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

## Product description
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Grey_Goose_(vodka)&action=edit&section=2)]

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grey_Goose_Vodka_IMG_3297.JPGA bottle of Grey Goose vodka, from 2010
The wheat used in the creation of Grey Goose vodka is grown in the [Picardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picardy) region of France. It is distilled in the [Northeast of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris), then sent to Cognac, France. Once received, the [distillate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distillate) is blended with a mix of [spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_water) and [bottled water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottled_water). Grey Goose uses "soft [winter wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_wheat)",[[10]](#cite_note-10) sown in October and harvested in August, which provides it with four additional months of growth in comparison to [summer wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_wheat).

Although Grey Goose distills its vodka from wheat, the product is overall [gluten-free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluten-free).[[11]](#cite_note-11) The distillation process removes the gluten from the final product.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

During the distilling process, Grey Goose uses [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme)[[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid_weasel_words)] to break down [carbohydrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbohydrates) into fermentable sugars. The [fermentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermentation) takes place continuously over six [cascading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascading) tanks, producing a 20-[proof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_(alcohol)) beer. The "wash" is then distilled into [spirits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquor) using a five-step process. The water used in the vodka comes from a natural spring 150 meters (500 feet) below the blending facility in Cognac, which is lined with [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone), providing [calcium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium)-rich spring water; that water is then filtered to remove impurities. After the filtration, the vodka is bottled in-plant. Grey Goose vodka is bottled with a replaceable [cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_cork) rather than a [screw cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screw_cap).[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-men-14)
